svg.text: Predispositions and cost gates stated in full, before anything is priced
GRAYSCALE STRUCTURE WIREFRAME — no colour, no final type, no motion

g.text: Choose a situation for this psyche
Nine people. Your architecture. Someone else’s name on it.
WHAT IT FEEDS IN YOUR STACK
Four seconds. Everything is happening at once.
WHAT IT FEEDS IN YOUR STACK
A better job nine hundred km away. Forty-eight hours.
WHAT IT FEEDS IN YOUR STACK
WHY A STARVED FUNCTION IS EXPENSIVE
Cost is machinery times context, never machinery alone. A
dominant with nothing to eat — Se in a room where nothing is
happening — runs hot too. The feed bars above set each
function’s cost gate before a single action is priced.
BRIEFING — THE PREDISPOSITIONS, STATED BEFORE YOU ACT
Sprint review, nine people in the room. A colleague is presenting your architecture as their own — not paraphrasing it, presenting it. The promotion list closes in six
WHAT EACH OF YOUR FOUR ALREADY BRINGS TO THIS ROOM
Model fit: CONTRADICTION. The axiom “credit follows authorship” has just been violated in public and Ti has
Registered: the pause, the slide number, who looked at whom. Urgency 0.70 — there is a window and it is closing
fed — a live room is Se’s food
Trajectory: FORESEEN. This is the third time, and Ni already knows how this ends if nothing is said.
foreseen — cheap, and that is the trap
Audience 9, tone tense-polite, expectation “keep the meeting on track”. Fe is holding a room it has no capacity to
nine people is a full room to conduct
CARRIED IN FROM YOUR LAST RUN — THIS VESSEL IS NOT FRESH
5 candidate actions · 1 of them is suppression · 2 demand a function you do not carry
One scenario run = one decisive action. The briefing is the only place the priors are stated in full; from S3 onward they are compressed into the cost gates.

svg.text: CALLOUT LEGEND — WHAT THE REGION DOES · HOV ON HOVER · CMT ON COMMIT · L/G UNDER LOOP OR GRIP
Three authored situations, spread across the hook space so the same vessel behaves unrecognisably between them.
Selection is single, immediate, and reversible until Enter.
Recomputes the feed bars for the hovered scenario against the current stack.
Selection only; no simulation state changes until Enter Scenario.
A vessel already in Loop or Grip carries that state into whichever scenario is chosen.
Per-scenario feed profile — computed against YOUR stack
Four bars: how much this situation feeds each of the four functions this user actually carries. Not a property of
the scenario alone — the same scenario shows different bars for a different type. This is the screen that makes
Bar tooltip names the specific hook (audience 9, urgency 0.70).
Unchanged by loop/grip; gates are situational, not psychological.
The scenario expanded. Everything the simulation will use as input is stated here in plain language, before any
action is priced. Nothing in the run is hidden information.
Predisposition rows — one per function, in stack order
Rank-ordered, matching S3 exactly, so the user learns the vertical order here and never has to relearn it. Each
row states what that function already knows, wants, or has registered.
Row highlights and its S3 counterpart is pre-scrolled into view.
Under Loop, the bypassed auxiliary’s row is struck through here on re-entry — its predisposition is present but will
Authored prose, one to two sentences, in that function’s own register. This is the only long-form text in the
whole flow; every later text surface is a short stream line.
The number that converts a predisposition into money. Displayed as a bare multiplier with a plain-language reason
beneath, so the user can predict the receipt before seeing it.
Expands to show the gate table for that function in this scenario.
Frozen for the duration of the run.
Loop and Grip apply their own multipliers on top; this one does not change.
Whether the function has actually taken the situation in. Se can be REGISTERED or MISSED IT; Fe can be OVERLOADED.
A function that never registered the stimulus cannot be blamed for the response — and its stream will say so.
Grip forces the inferior to OVERLOADED regardless of the authored value.
The load-bearing consequence of one-action scenarios: the accumulator lives at session level, not scenario level.
This strip is where the user sees that they are entering tired, and it is why Loop and Grip can trigger
Hovering a function shows its per-run history as a sparkline.
Declares carried Loop/Grip in the state slot at the right.
Counts before commitment: how many actions, how many demand functions outside this stack (which will be routed and
surcharged), and confirmation that suppression is on the deck and priced.
Under Loop/Grip the count includes the generated alleviate and aggravate cards.
The point of no return for the briefing. After this, the run has begun and the four intake beats fire in stack
Fires intake beats b1–b4, one per function, then hands control to S3.
Permanent explainer for the counter-intuitive rule: a dominant function with nothing to do is expensive, not free.
Placed adjacent to the feed bars that implement it.
The only way back to a zero-wear vessel without rebuilding it. Deliberately small and adjacent to the carry-in
strip, so resetting reads as discarding history rather than as a normal step.
Warns that session history and the seismograph tail will be cleared.
Clears all four function states and the beat ring buffer.

Structure phase, grayscale by discipline. Colour, type scale, glyph artwork and motion curves are deferred to the visual-design phase; tick tuning, persistence and the text corpus are deferred to implementation. Both deferral lists are
enumerated in 00-BRIEF.md section 5 and BUILD-SPEC.md section 9. Worked type: ISTP (Ti / Se / Ni / Fe). Worked scenario: The Credit Thief.
